title: The Army just used a 20-kilowatt laser to take out three drones
raw_text: This week, the US Army used a high-energy multipurpose laser to shoot down three drones near the US-Mexico border, which official reports claimed were “posing a physical threat to US military personnel and CBP partners,” referring to Customs and Border Patrol. The operation took place between the night of August 25 and the early morning of August 26 in the vicinity of the Rio Grande Valley in Texas and was led by the Joint Task Force Southern Border (JTF-SB), which operates under US Northern Command. Authorities confirmed that, during the operation, agents used technology derived from the Army’s High-Energy Multipurpose Laser (AMP-HEL) system, a military program focused on implementing high-energy lasers for new defense capabilities. Available information suggests that this initiative began in September 2025, when AeroVironment, a company specializing in defense technology, delivered the first two functional prototypes of these laser-based weapons to the US Armed Forces. Two new, improved systems were delivered as the program was expanded in December of the same year. According to the manufacturer, this particular platform, called the Locust Laser Weapon System, is designed to be mounted on military vehicles, as the Army has done with the versions it has received. raw_text: Veel mensen gebruiken AI als vraagbaak: je start een chat, stelt een vraag, krijgt antwoord en begint de volgende keer weer met een nieuwe chat. Een AI-assistent oftewel een ‘custom agent’ werkt net anders: het is een digitale collega die je inwerkt op een specifieke taak. De grootste winst? Die ligt in het automatiseren van repeterende werkzaamheden, zodat er meer tijd overblijft voor strategie, creativiteit en contact met jouw doelgroep. In dit artikel lees je wat een AI-assistent is en hoe je er zelf een kunt inrichten om efficiënter te kunnen werken. Wat is een AI-assistent? Een AI-assistent kun je inrichten om een specifieke taak zo goed mogelijk uit te voeren. In plaats van bij iedere nieuwe chat opnieuw uit te leggen wat je wilt, geef je de assistent vooraf context, instructies en relevante documenten mee. Daardoor begrijpt het programma jouw werkwijze beter en kan het jou consistenter en beter ondersteunen. De AI voert geen autonome taken uit zoals een AI-agent, maar werkt alleen met jouw input. Waar te beginnen? Het kan ingewikkeld klinken, maar om een assistent te kunnen inrichten hoef je geen ICT- of programmeringskennis te hebben. Vrijwel alle AI-platformen bieden de mogelijkheid om een eigen assistent te bouwen. Hierbij is de start het meest belangrijk: een AI-assistent is namelijk zo slim als de informatie waarmee je hem voedt. title: Art for Everyone: How Public Libraries Expand Access
raw_text: Introducing children to viewing, creating, and enjoying art at a young age helps them appreciate it throughout their lives. Some children are exposed to various forms of art because it is part of their daily life or because they have easy access to museums and galleries in their community. But in many areas across the country, access to museums and art galleries can be cost prohibitive. That is where the public library comes in! While some museums, including the Smithsonian Institution in Washington, D.C., offer free admission, millions of people across the country do not have easy access to them. According to the 2024 Annual Survey of Museum-Goers from the American Alliance of Museums and Wilkening Consulting, museum admission costs vary widely, from a few dollars to $40–$50 per adult at some institutions. Among U.S. adults who visit museums at least occasionally, cost was the number one barrier to visiting more often. Among frequent museum-goers, younger adults were twice as likely as seniors to be concerned about admission costs. In response to those barriers, and in an effort to enrich and inspire customers of all ages, many library systems have stepped up to provide access to art in a variety of forms. Borrowing Art from the Library Brooklyn Public Library in New York recently launched a lending program featuring art by local artists. raw_text: Welcome to American Libraries’ 2026 Library Design Showcase, our annual celebration of new and renovated libraries across the US and Canada. The word welcome appeared in many of this year’s submissions, reflecting a growing understanding that in anxious times, the library is a place that should feel good: safe, comfortable, well-lit, plugged in, and deeply connected to its surroundings. More than two-thirds of this year’s 15 selections are renovations or adaptive reuse projects. Libraries of all types are finding ways to acknowledge historical and environmental realities, embrace natural elements and cultural identities, evolve traditions, and build in flexibility to account for the unexpected. Read on for snapshots of these communities in motion. Natural immersion Maplewood (N.J.) Memorial Library Adjacent to a historic park, with protected natural areas on all sides, this 1955 masonry structure had nowhere to expand but up. The new, light-filled second floor features bird-safe glass, wood battens, and green roofs for a treehouse feel. The all-electric building, the first LEED Gold–certified library in New Jersey, includes solar panels that offset more than half of the library’s energy use. title: Secrets of Effective Upskilling
raw_text: This is an excerpt from Upskilling for Library Workers: A Guide for Future-Ready Professionals by Ann Medaille (ALA Editions, 2026). With the advent of new technologies and rapid social and economic shifts, library workers’ jobs are being transformed. Compared with a decade ago, library workers now spend more time consulting on complex research tools, teaching digital literacy classes, supporting virtual learning environments, helping users troubleshoot devices, and codesigning projects with community partners. The pace at which library staffers are called upon to learn new skills is accelerating, and workers may struggle to keep up. In addition, automation and artificial intelligence (AI) are altering many aspects of work. In the long run, technological innovations have the potential to increase productivity and lead to more interesting kinds of work, but in the short term, they often cause disruptions that can be difficult for workers to navigate. To address these changes—and manage the anxieties that come along with them—workers need constant support for skill development. While corporations may embrace upskilling to stay competitive, libraries will have to support upskilling to remain relevant. Library leaders are under greater pressure to respond rapidly to changing social and economic conditions and demonstrate that their libraries make a difference in their communities. title: Hold the Phone
raw_text: Since fall 2024, each school day at Grant High School in Portland, Oregon, has started the same way: Roughly 2,100 students line up to place their phones in gray and green Yondr pouches—the kind live performers use to prevent audience members from recording—as they enter the building. From the morning bell to dismissal, phones are sealed and can be unlocked only with special magnets near the school’s exits as students leave for the day. The high school’s effort to limit phone use on campus has received support from its educators, who say classroom engagement is on the rise, and mixed reviews from students, who dislike being cut off from their devices. But there’s been one unexpected outcome of the policy: More students are spending time in the library, where they’re browsing the collection or hanging out during free periods, says teacher-librarian Paige Battle. “They’re checking out more books, and I feel like that’s been so important in their education,” Battle says. “We’re seeing studies about students, even adults, not having the reading stamina they’ve had in the past, so I’ve been encouraged by this increase.” Roughly six in 10 parents of an 11- or 12-year-old say their child owns a smartphone, according to a 2025 Pew Research Center survey . And as more schools across the country enact phone-free policies—29 states and the District of Columbia have instituted bell-to-bell phone-free policies so far—many school libraries are experiencing a surge in popularity. title: Newsmaker: Min Jin Lee
raw_text: Min Jin Lee has notched career milestones that few authors reach. Her immigration saga Pachinko was both a National Book Award finalist and a New York Times Top 10 Best Book of 2017, and it was adapted into a television series of the same name for Apple TV. Lee is also a Guggenheim fellow and the first Korean American to hold the role of New York State author laureate. Her latest title, American Hagwon (Cardinal, September), examines the influence of Korean “cram schools” among families in the Korean diaspora. American Libraries spoke with Lee ahead of her appearance at the American Library Association’s 2026 Annual Conference and Exhibition in Chicago. She discussed her new book, the library that shaped her, and her antidote to book bans. What inspired you to focus on the education system as it relates to the movements of a middle-class Korean American family in American Hagwon ? My research process involved all these interviews—I’ve done hundreds of them, probably almost 1,000 at this point—and every single time I talked to somebody, they would mention their education path. It was such an important and controversial subject. I thought, if I had to think about the most important value for Koreans, especially in the diaspora, what would I write about? Education turned out to be a beast, because people have lots of feelings about it. In the book, the Koh family loses wealth and status as they weather betrayal and financial crises. title: Mall Wonder
raw_text: After serving its community for nearly 45 years in the same building, Escondido (Calif.) Public Library closed in April 2025 for an $11.6 million renovation. It was important to us, as the city’s lone library, to preserve access during construction. So one month later, our library opened a temporary location in a very different kind of facility: the nearby North County Mall, where services and collections were spread across six storefronts, including a former Abercrombie & Fitch clothing store. Of course, moving a library takes more than a month. Our planning took more than a year and required staff to work under tight deadlines, limited budgets, and high expectations. Here’s how we did it, and what we learned from the process. Choosing a location. It’s essential to consider whether the new location will match, improve upon, or limit access. Retailers and mall operators have already studied traffic patterns, visibility, parking, and nearby amenities. Leverage that knowledge to evaluate access. In our case, the public benefited from a highway and bus stop near the mall, and adjacency to a city park. The arrangement also gave the mall a stable civic tenant and created natural cross-traffic between library patrons and shoppers. The mall was not just available space; it was a location where public access, economic development, and community visibility could overlap. title: Dismantling Disinformation
raw_text: Library workers are well aware of the effects of book bans and censorship. Propaganda and disinformation are the flipside of the same coin. Understanding the complex relationships among these interrelated processes is more critical than ever, especially as libraries explore possible solutions and responses. The following books show how disinformation can lead to censorship and how censorship can, in turn, allow disinformation to thrive. Book Bans, Disinformation, and Cultural Erasure: The Censor­ship Movement in Libraries, Schools, and Society By Paul T. Jaeger Jaeger situates the current book-banning movement within a larger social and political effort to erase marginalized communities and culture. He provides clear definitions and examples of these processes and goals, including the roles played by technological progress and economic inequity. With accessible references (like the Beatles, Dungeons & Dragons, and Holmes and Watson) and nuanced examinations of McCarthyism, the history of libraries, and the myth of neutrality, this is a recommended read for anyone interested in a more expansive understanding of current First Amendment challenges. title: A Sense of Purpose
raw_text: When it comes to building resilient and equitable communities, libraries are natural leaders. We provide places where neighbors meet, learn, and support one another; where sustainability education becomes action; and where residents can find year-round climate refuge. When communities are resilient, they are better able to overcome barriers. The Obama Presidential Center (OPC) branch of Chicago Public Library (CPL) is an example of a library that strengthens the social infrastructure that underpins resilience. CPL Commissioner Chris Brown describes the branch as a civic platform for residents, artists, educators, and organizations to cocreate the life of the library and its surrounding public spaces. Though just 5,000 square feet, OPC was designed to spark connection, invite conversation, and inspire activities that encourage ­socialization and enjoyment. The branch partners with such nonprofits as the Art Institute of Chicago, the literary arts group StoryStudio Chicago , and the artist-led alt_Chicago . OPC is a striking example of how libraries do not just serve resilient communities, they help create them. On the Gulf Coast, sustainability is a daily requirement. Lindsay Cronk, dean of Tulane University Libraries in New Orleans, has shared that the library’s partnership with Keep Louisiana Beautiful , a state program, helps connect students, faculty, and staff with opportunities for conservation, beautification, recycling, and environmental action. raw_text: Muziekmaatschappijen Sony Music Group, Universal Music Group en Warner Music Group leiden de investeringsronde van 76 miljoen dollar in het Britse Stability AI. De makers van Stable Diffusion behoorden in 2022 tot de eerste groep bedrijven en onderzoekslabs die GenAI binnen handbereik van het grote publiek bracht. Dit bedrijf specialiseerde zich specifiek in text-to-image beeldgeneratie. Deze ronde in de zin dat de nieuwe deelnemers eraan voornamelijk uit de entertaimentindustrie komen. Ook Electronic Arts en reclamreus WPP storten dollars. Een brede waaiers zittende zittende, voornamelijk Amerikaanse, investeerders doet ook mee. Stability AI gaat de miljoenen dollars uit deze, nu pas, Series B-ronde gebruiken om zijn suite van creatieve productietools voor muziek, gaming en entertainment uit te breiden. Daarnaast gaat een deel naar toegepast onderzoek en een ander deel naar het vergroten van het commerciële apparaat. In mei bracht de modellenbouwer Stable Audio 3.0 uit, een familie van open-weight muziekmodellen getraind op volledig gelicentieerde data, met een DAW-plugin voor integratie in professionele workflows. title: Hamburg wil Smart Glasses in zwembaden en OV verbieden
raw_text: De Hamburgse rood-groene coalitie en Die Linke willen brillen met ingebouwde camera’s — zogenaamde Smart Glasses — weren uit bepaalde delen van het openbare leven. Het doel is vooral om de privacy van mensen beter te beschermen tegen heimelijke foto- en video-opnamen. Het voorgestelde verbod zou gelden in alle gemeentelijke zwembaden van Hamburg, waaronder zwem- en rustgedeelten ligweiden, kleedkamers, douches, sanitaire ruimtes en sauna’s. SPD en Groenen willen het verbod daarnaast uitbreiden naar bussen en treinen van het openbaar vervoer. Volgens hen moeten reizigers erop kunnen vertrouwen dat ze niet ongemerkt worden gefilmd. Het probleem met Smart Glasses is volgens de initiatiefnemers dat ze nauwelijks te onderscheiden zijn van een gewone bril. Bij een smartphone is meestal duidelijk wanneer iemand aan het filmen is; bij een bril met een ingebouwde camera is dat veel moeilijker te zien. Als voorbeeld wordt een Hamburgse vrouw genoemd die tijdens een gesprek aan de Alster ongemerkt met een Smart Glass werd gefilmd. De beelden verschenen later in een TikTok-video die duizenden keren werd bekeken. De Groenen en SPD willen bovendien dat er op nationaal niveau regels voor Smart Glasses komen. Vooral gezichtsherkenning door particulieren in de openbare ruimte wordt als problematisch gezien. title: Prijs­kaart­je cloud stijgt elk jaar met 9 procent
raw_text: Cloud- en softwareprijzen stegen volgens Europees onderzoek van Cigref de voorbije drie jaar gemiddeld met 8,7 procent per jaar. Voor de komende vijf jaar verwacht de Franse cio-vereniging zelfs een jaarlijkse stijging van 12 procent. De prijsdruk geeft extra gewicht aan de Europese discussie over digitale soevereiniteit, onder meer via de voorgestelde Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA). Als organisaties evenveel cloud en software blijven afnemen, zou de prijsinflatie over vijf jaar gemiddeld 140 miljard euro extra per jaar kosten. Daarvan zou volgens Cigref, de Franse vereniging van CIO’s, ongeveer 93 miljard euro jaarlijks Europa verlaten. De cijfers kwamen ter sprake tijdens een persbriefing van Beltug, de Belgische vereniging van CIO’s en digitale technologieleiders, over de Cloud and AI Development Act. Met ai als verklaring Leveranciers verwijzen geregeld naar nieuwe ai-functionaliteiten om hogere prijzen te verantwoorden. Dat argument wordt volgens Cigref in ongeveer 40 procent van de gevallen gebruikt. Maar de productiviteitswinst die daar tegenover staat, overtuigt gebruikers nog niet massaal. Bij bijna 60 procent van de respondenten wordt die winst op korte en middellange termijn vooral als theoretisch beschouwd. Organisaties vangen de hogere facturen vooral op door hun budgetten te verhogen of middelen elders te verschuiven. Cigref raamt die compensatie op 108 miljard euro per jaar. title: China-linked hackers backdoored executives' laptops via USB, exploiting a fix companies had but weren't using
raw_text: A Chinese state-linked hacking group compromised executive laptops at an agricultural industry conference on Hainan Island this spring — not through phishing or a network breach, but by breaking into hotel rooms and booting the machines from a USB stick while the executives were at dinner. CrowdStrike, which tracks the group as OVERCAST PANDA , disclosed the campaign in its 2026 Threat Hunting Report and detailed the operation's timeline in an interview with VentureBeat at Fal.Con 2026: an intruder entered one room at around 8 p.m. local time and a second room by 9:57 p.m., writing a backdoor called FlowCloud directly to each laptop's storage before rebooting the machines and leaving. There was no network intrusion, no phishing email, and no credential stolen through a login page. The report dates the intrusions to between March and May 2026, and the timestamps come from Adam Meyers, CrowdStrike's senior vice president of counter adversary operations, who cleared them for publication in the VentureBeat interview. CrowdStrike's OverWatch team disrupted the intrusions and assessed that OVERCAST PANDA will almost certainly continue. FlowCloud itself predates this campaign by years: Proofpoint documented it in 2020 , delivered by phishing to U.S. utilities, and NTT Security's SOC has tracked USB-delivered infections at overseas branches of Japanese organizations since early 2022.
